title.narrative: Lessons Learned and Policy Recommendations for Critical Issues in 2026 on Peace, Security and illicit crops in Colombia

description.narrative: The project's purpose is to develop and socialize strategic roadmaps and public policy recommendations on critical issues related to peace, security and illicit crops through practical research exercises and closed-door exchanges with key practitioners (including current and former public officials, negotiators, experts and local leaders), with the aim of informing the 2026 electoral debate and helping mitigate the current instability affecting the peace and security agenda. The proposed project includes three components aimed at generating evidence-based roadmaps for the next national government on territorial security and illicit crop dynamics: (i) a diagnostic component at both the national and territorial levels to assess the current situation and the impacts of actions undertaken in key peace and security areas; (ii) an analytical component aimed at identifying lessons learned from past security and drug policies; and (iii) a forward-looking component that formulates evidence-based recommendations for future presidential candidates and decision-makers in 2026, grounded in the diagnoses and insights gained regarding Colombia’s peace, security and illicit crops policies. The overall approach will be carried out through a variety of methodologies and activities, with a strong emphasis on high-level, closed-door dialogue and exchange with key practitioners, experts and communities. For the purposes of this project, "practitioners and experts" refers to current and former public officials at both national and territorial levels, social leaders with experience in peace, security and illicit crops-related initiatives, members of international organizations with territorial presence, private sector representatives, and academics. The findings of this project, across its two lines of analysis (illicit crops and territorial security), will be shared and discussed progressively with presidential candidates and their technical teams.
